name: Tacunyape
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.note: No descriptive references; only Loukotka 1968 pp. 112-113 cited for subclassification; AES status extinct.
Nothing; reproduces the Nimuendajú 1932 wordlist and cites only that source; claims extinction in the early 1950s (Nimuendajú 1932 says the tribe died out by c. 1900 with one non-speaking survivor).

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt. 1932. Idiomas indígenas del Brasil. Revista del Instituto de Etnología de la Universidad Nacional de Tucumán 2(2): 543-618. Section 'Die Takunyape', pp. 543-547 (German), wordlist p. 547.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Four pages of ethnohistory plus c. 40 words recalled from memory by three settlers (Accioly, de Castro, Pinheiro) decades after the tribe died out; Nimuendajú warns 'deren Aussprache jedoch wohl recht mangelhaft gewesen sein dürfte' and that he knows no other records. Forms are printed with acute accents (kuarí, tupá, amán, yapepó, iká, marapé, tapií, akikí, arapayá, irirí, tairí, katú), mostly on the final vowel, but there is no diacritics key for this section and no remark on accent. (The 'tonischer accent' keys on pp. 573 and 590 belong to the Tukuna and Içana/Uaupés sections, not…

sources.citation: Coudreau, Henri. 1897. Voyage au Xingú (30 mai 1896 - 26 octobre 1896). Paris: Lahure.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Coudreau met the last c. 40 Takunyapé in 1894-96 (Nimuendajú 1932: 546 cites him pp. 20, 33); his Xingu volumes carry vocabularies of other tribes and could conceivably hold a few Takunyapé words with accent marks. Nimuendajú, who read it, says he knew of no other record, and Loukotka cites only Nimuendajú, so the chance is low.
